title: Titrating ethanoic acid with NaOH
subject: chemistry
statement: {Va} mL of {Ca} mol/L ethanoic acid (Ka = {Ka}) is titrated with {Cb} mol/L NaOH. (a) Find the initial pH. (b) What volume of NaOH reaches the equivalence point? (c) Find the pH halfway to equivalence. (d) Find the pH at the equivalence point.

parts.hint: A weak acid: Ka = x^2 / (Ca - x).

steps.say: Set up Ka equals x squared over C a minus x and solve for x.
pH is minus log ten of the hydrogen ion concentration.

parts.hint: Moles of NaOH equal moles of acid.

steps.say: At equivalence, C b times V equals C a times V a.
Halfway, the acid and its salt are equal, so pH equals pKa.

parts.hint: Only ethanoate is left: it's a weak base, Kb = Kw/Ka.

steps.say: At equivalence the volume has doubled, so the salt's concentration halves.
Hydroxide comes from the square root of K b times C.
Then pH is fourteen minus pOH.

summary: Equivalence: the salt is a weak base, so pH > 7
